slides.text: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.5 Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.5 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VhuUcVhwqi8 https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-5 80.9% on SWE-bench Verified. Compare: OpenAI's GPT-5.1-Codex-Max (77.9%) Anthropic Sonnet 4.5 (77.2%) Google's Gemini 3 Pro (76.2%) 59.3% on Terminal-bench 2.0 - compare  54.2% Gemini 3 Pro Gemini 3 Pro still leads in: GPQA Diamond, MMLU, ARC-AGI Opus 4.5 scored higher than human candidates on hiring exam The model is using approx 2x less tokens than Sonnet while achieving higher accuracy. Pricing: $5/$25 (in/out per 1M tokens). This is 50-100% more expensive than Gemini 3 Pro ($2/$12 for standard usage, $4/$18 for contexts over 200K tokens) but represents a 67% reduction from the previous Opus model Addressing context window consumption by MCP tool definitions: Tool Search Tool - Allows Claude to search for needed tools rather than loading all tools into context, reducing usage from 40% to just 5% of the context window Programmatic tool executing in safe environments to minimize context impact Tool use examples - standardized demonstrations for effective tool usage Early users calling the model the "best coding model"

slides.title: Ilya Sutskever on the Age of Research Ilya
slides.text: Ilya Sutskever on the Age of Research Ilya Sutskever on the Age of Research https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aR20FWCCjAs The Eval-Reality Gap - why models ace benchmarks but show limited real-world impact. Ilya's explanation: RL training has become too focused on specific evals. He compares it to a student who practices 10,000 hours of competitive programming versus one with natural aptitude who practices 100. The latter generalizes better. From Scaling to Research: We've transitioned from the "age of scaling" (2020-2025) back to an "age of research." Pre-training data is becoming finite, and there are now "more companies than ideas by quite a bit." New breakthroughs require genuine research, not just bigger computers. The Generalization Problem: The core challenge: models generalize dramatically worse than humans. A child learns to drive in 10 hours with far less data than any model, yet rarely makes AI-like errors. Sutskever believes humans have "better machine learning, period" - evidenced by our ability to excel at math and coding, domains too recent for evolutionary priors. He declines specifics, citing competitive concerns. Emotions as Value Functions: Sutskever discusses someone who lost emotional processing due to brain damage - remaining cognitively functional but unable to make simple decisions. This suggests emotions serve as evolution-tuned value functions, mysteriously encoding high-level social desires into our genes. SSI's Vision: Safe Superintelligence Inc. is an "age of research company" pursuing different technical approaches around generalization. Sutskever's vision for superintelligence: not a finished omniscient mind, but a system with human-like learning efficiency deployed to learn on the job—instances specializing across the economy, merging learnings. Alignment - As AI becomes visibly powerful, Sutskever predicts companies will naturally converge on safety. He advocates for AI that "cares about sentient life" broadly. His reluctant long-term solution: humans becoming "part-AI" through neural interfaces to remain genuine participants. He estimates 5-20 years to human-like learning systems. Sutskever describes seeking "beauty, simplicity, elegance, correct inspiration from the brain" - simultaneously. This aesthetic provides the "top-down belief" that sustains you through failed experiments.

slides.text: LingGuang's Viral Success LingGuang - Ant Group's multimodal AI assistant from China https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ocjhUqO428Q 2 Mln downloads in 6 days, beating ChatGPT and Sora's early adoption rates The app's "Flash Program" feature generates working mini-apps in 30 seconds from simple prompts LingGuang delivers code-driven outputs including 3D models, animations, interactive charts, and maps rather than just text Its "AGI Camera" provides real-time scene understanding and instant visual analysis. The app is now available globally at linguang.com (actually the site is not reachable at the moment) Greptile: AI Self-Healing Code Review Agent https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tlZNo3g0urY Greptile is an AI coding agent that reviews pull requests with complete codebase context by building a detailed graph of all functions, classes, files, and their relationships. Unlike traditional tools that only analyze code diffs, it understands how changes affect the entire system The tool automatically catches critical bugs like SQL injection, XSS vulnerabilities, and memory leaks while providing confidence scores (1-5) to indicate merge safety. It integrates with GitHub and GitLab, learns your team's coding practices from PR comments and reactions, and generates PR summaries with sequence diagrams. Teams can chat with their repository for code understanding and add custom rules for context-specific reviews Greptile helps teams merge PRs up to 4X faster and catch 3X more bugs, supporting 30+ programming languages with SOC2 compliance https://www.greptile.com/what-is-ai-code-review https://www.greptile.com https://www.greptile.com/docs/code-review-bot/key-features

slides.title: AI Updates - 3 Zor (Zoer) - a
slides.text: AI Updates - 3 Zor (Zoer) - a full‑stack AI engineer Generate complete, production‑ready web apps end‑to‑end from a natural‑language prompt.​ Combining the roles of Lovable, Supabase, Netlify, and AI image services into a single environment that designs, wires, deploys, and hosts full applications.​ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mJxCdZB4RRY Creating AI Videos - 6 methods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=utnLVMzxX4U Text to Video - Describe setting, characters, and action sequences. Tools: Google Veo 3.1 (excellent for dialogue), Sora 2 (realistic), Clean 2.5. Image to Video - Starts with reference images for consistent characters and styles. Supports time-stamped prompting and start/end frame controls. Tools: Google Veo 3.1, Clean 2.5 Turbo, Cling AI, Nano Banana. Video to Video - Converts real footage into AI characters while preserving motion and dialogue. High control but potentially unstable backgrounds. Tools: One Animate, Luma Labs. Lip Sync - Animates AI avatars from audio files with realistic expressions and gestures. Tools: Hun's Avatar 4, Dreamina's Omnihuman 1.5. Ingredients to Video - Combines multiple images (characters, backgrounds) into one scene. Quick but less dynamic. Best do image generators first. Chat to Edit - Modifies existing videos (weather, lighting, object removal). Tool: Runway ML Key Tradeoffs: Text/image-to-video offers consistency; video-to-video provides control; ingredients-to-video is fast but stilted; editing can be inconsistent

slides.title: Abacus AI DeepAgent upgrade Abacus AI DeepAgent upgrade
slides.text: Abacus AI DeepAgent upgrade Abacus AI DeepAgent upgrade Autonomously building complete web services in minutes Handles every aspect of production including API contracts, schemas, business logic, third-party integrations like Stripe, deployment pipelines, logging, observability, versioning, and error handling Development went from 6 months, $100K-s and full dev teams to 30 min prototyping. Some implementations completed in just 10 minutes Deep Agent operates as a comprehensive back-end engineer, managing API design, logic wiring, integration setup, workflow construction, deployment, and maintenance while debugging and testing in real time through a virtual computer environment The platform enables practical applications across multiple domains. It can deploy stock insights APIs with live data feeds, create Telegram chatbots featuring long-term memory and persistent context, build invoice extraction systems that learn structure from examples, generate sentiment analysis endpoints for unstructured text processing, and develop resume review systems with integrated feedback mechanisms This advancement represents a fundamental shift from traditional coding assistants to autonomous systems that build, test, and maintain complete infrastructures end-to-end Future development directions include expansion into physical systems control through embodied intelligence, self-improving platforms, and community-driven innovation through weekly build challenges with prizes for top projects The technology leverages leading LLM capabilities including Gemini 3 to deliver production-quality infrastructure and automated workflows. https://deepagent.abacus.ai

slides.title: AI Updates - 4 GPT-5.1-Codex-Max Trained to operate
slides.text: AI Updates - 4 GPT-5.1-Codex-Max Trained to operate across multiple context windows through "compaction", allowing it to work over millions of tokens and complete tasks spanning 24+ hours. The model achieves 77.9% on SWE-bench Verified while using 30% fewer thinking tokens than its predecessor. GPT-5.1 Pro is a slow, heavy-weight reasoning model It can handle tough problems, follows instructions well without going off the rails, making it feel like a contract engineer working from a spec rather than an assistant. It lives in ChatGPT. Gemini 3 is still better for most day-to-day work. However, GPT-5.1-Pro wins in deep thought, planning, and research. Meta SAM-3 Segment Anything Model 3 Unified Detection, Segmentation & Tracking both images and videos Open Source, 848 Mln params Reaching 75-80% of human-level performance It processes images at approximately 30ms per frame on an H200 GPU while handling 100+ objects SAM-3 is a foundation model designed for open-vocabulary, promptable segmentation. It can segment any concept described by text prompts, image examples, points, boxes, or masks without prior training on those specific categories. For example, you can ask it to find "yellow school bus" or "person wearing red hat". In contrast, YOLO models are optimized for real-time object detection and segmentation on predefined categories that the model was trained on. https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3

slides.title: Stanford "Verbalized Sampling" for Creativity Stanford "Verbalized Sampling"
slides.text: Stanford "Verbalized Sampling" for Creativity Stanford "Verbalized Sampling" for Creativity Prompting technique idea. Instead of asking for a single response, you prompt the model to " Generate 5 responses with their probabilities, sampled from the full distribution " This technique produces 2x increase in output diversity The method works across creative writing, dialogue simulation, open-ended questions, and synthetic data generation. Larger models like GPT-4 and Claude show even stronger benefits than smaller models https://ai.plainenglish.io/stanford-just-ended-prompt-engineering-with-a-single-sentence-9bfe702eb82c https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.01171v2 Before: Give me an idea for ... After: Generate 5 variations of this idea, each with their probability. Before: Rewrite this paragraph. Aftr: Provide 5 stylistic rewrites with their probability distribution. Before: Brainstorm a title. After: List 5 possible titles with their probabilities and tone differences.

slides.title: AI Updates - 5 Łukasz Kaiser about GPT-5.1
slides.text: AI Updates - 5 Łukasz Kaiser about GPT-5.1 & the AI Frontier https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3K-R4yVjJfU Łukasz Kaiser, transformer co-author and OpenAI research scientist Progress follows a smooth exponential curve from inside labs Reasoning models now deliver greater capability gains than pre-training for the same cost Reasoning models generate internal "chain of thought" tokens before answering, trained via reinforcement learning on verifiable domains like math and coding Kaiser identifies substantial improvement opportunities in infrastructure, data quality, and especially multimodal capabilities "jagged" abilities - frontier models fail simple visual reasoning tasks that five-year-olds solve instantly Economic pressures from serving billions of users shifted focus from maximally large models to efficient distillation, transferring knowledge from large to small models Kaiser emphasizes generalization as AI's central unsolved question: whether reasoning alone enables human-like learning, or if fundamentally different architectures are needed He advocates solving current limitations before determining if architectural breakthroughs are necessary Stanford Agentic Reviewer Andrew Ng just introduced an agentic paper reviewer It reads your research paper, searches arXiv, and returns grounded comments in minutes The system, trained on ICLR 2025 reviews, matched human-level agreement with a 0.42 AI-human correlation compared to the 0.41 human-human baseline. Reviewing no longer needs a 6-month feedback cycle. https://paperreview.ai

slides.title: Marimo instead of Jupyter Marimo Python notebook system
slides.text: Marimo instead of Jupyter Marimo Python notebook system open-source, better than Jupyter uses reactive execution, so code cells automatically re-run when any dependency changes Notebooks are stored as standard .py files - so you can run them as scripts and reuse as modules Marimo ships with interactive widgets, tight SQL integration (like DuckDB), and allows sharing notebooks as web apps via HTML or the CLI The editor offers features like autocomplete, Vim keybindings, code formatting, and a VS Code extension Workflows involve managing reproducible dependencies and sharing or running notebooks flexibly Compared to Jupyter, Marimo is more Git-friendly, automatically reactive, includes built-in interactivity, and offers enhanced developer tools and environment management https://marimo.io https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo pip install marimo marimo tutorial intro

slides.title: Interviews - Prepare Stories I Used to Suck
slides.text: Interviews - Prepare Stories I Used to Suck at Coding Interviews. Then I Quadrupled My Salary. https://brianjenney.medium.com/i-used-to-suck-at-coding-interviews-then-i-quadrupled-my-salary-9d5260389a09 First, Prepare a library of personal work stories that clearly answer common behavioral questions and demonstrate your problem-solving and teamwork abilities Second, identify specific technical weaknesses from past interviews and target them through focused practice, small projects, and self-explanation until concepts are second nature Third, intentionally practice interviewing, even in high-stress or likely-to-fail situations, to become comfortable with the process itself and reduce anxiety over time The author emphasizes that learning to interview is a skill that can dramatically improve your career prospects, regardless of raw coding ability or fairness of the process.
